summary: Backend-only verification of the @birthright.org -> @birthright.live domain migration. New test suite /app/backend/tests/test_iter45_domain_migration.py (16 tests) passes 100%: all five seeded accounts log in on the new domain with correct roles (admin/participant/facilitator/facilitator/readonly_admin) and /api/auth/me agrees; all five old @birthright.org emails now correctly return 401; counsel read flows (GET /api/legal/pages, POST redline comment, list-verify) work and apply-roundtrip is still 403 {readonly:true}; admin GET /api/admin/settings/counsel returns email='counsel@birthright.live', rotate to temp pw + login + restore to counsel-review-2026 all succeed (counsel login re-verified 200 after teardown); doc checks pass for test_credentials.md, 00a-counsel-user-guide.md and LEGAL_BRIEFING_FOR_COUNSEL.md (no stale @birthright.org emails). Regression: the existing counsel suite (iter32/33/34/35/36/36b/38) FAILS as-checked-in (15 failed, 38 errors) purely because every fixture hardcodes @birthright.org credentials. To prove there is no functional regression I copied those 7 files to /tmp/migcheck with the domain rewritten (originals untouched) and ran them: 65/65 PASSED. So the migration itself is clean; only test fixtures need updating.
